results.summary_before: This project is a DDR throughput and flop aperture test that grabs data on every clock edge with varying positive pulse widths. It uses positive edge detectors on the clock and its complement to generate two pulses per period, with pulse width adjusted by the number of inverters. The design outputs the captured data and includes a normal flop for comparison. Testing requires an Analog Discovery 3, and the documentation is minimal, with the author stating it works 'badly probably'.

results.summary_before: This is a Simon Says memory game where the player repeats an ever-growing sequence of colors shown on four LEDs, each with a corresponding tone, and the current level is shown on a two-digit seven-segment display. It uses four buttons, four LEDs, an optional speaker and a multiplexed seven-segment display, and can be tested with a dedicated Simon Says Pmod or with discrete components. A Wokwi simulation with wiring diagram is provided. Silicon testing confirmed it works as expected with the Pmod when the design is reset after selection.

results.summary_before: This design controls the segments of a 7-segment display, including the decimal point, based on input signals. It was created as part of an IEEE-sponsored Tiny Tapeout workshop in San Diego in November 2024, in collaboration with UCSD. The design is tested by toggling the inputs and observing the segments turn on and off. It requires an external 7-segment display for output.
